title: Embedding staleness & cache fallback — hosting options discussion
summary: Introductory discovery focusing on embedding freshness, caching strategies, and tradeoffs between Redwood hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Customer is evaluating vector DB integrations and needs recommendations on staleness windows, cache invalidation, and throughput scaling for a near-real-time recommendation product. Agreed next steps: benchmark plan, security pack, pricing scenarios for Dedicated vs Private.
topics: hosting decision: hosted vs dedicated vs private
vector DB integration (existing: Milvus, considering Pinecone)
cache strategies, staleness windows, prefix/KV caching
next_steps: Samir to share Redwood-hosted vs dedicated vs private one-pager and pricing scenarios (by 2027-01-04)
Jenna to propose a benchmark plan and test harness for our throughput/staleness matrix (by 2027-01-07)
Priya/Liam to share sample traffic shape and current embedding refresh cadence (by 2026-12-27)
Redwood to provide SOC2/security docs and network architecture sketch for VPC deploy (by 2027-01-06)
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting once benchmark plan agreed (tentative week of 2027-01-11)
action_items: Samir Patel: email hosting comparison + ballpark pricing — due 2027-01-04
Jenna Morales: draft benchmark plan (throughput x staleness sweep) — due 2027-01-07
Priya Rao: export 24h traffic histogram + current embed refresh job schedule — due 2026-12-27
Liam Chen: confirm compliance contacts and residency requirements — due 2027-01-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Liam (AetherData CTO), Priya (Lead ML Eng), Marco (Head of ML)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick off — can folks say who they are real quick?
[00:08] Liam: yeah liam here, cto at aetherdata, thanks — quick ask, mostly around recommender freshness and cost.
[00:12] Priya: priya — i run the embedding pipeline, we currently push embeddings every ~10 minutes for hot content and hourly for cold.
[00:18] Marco: marco — head of ml, focusing on quality tradeoffs and SLA.
[00:22] Jenna: thanks team, jenna from redwood, i'll focus on technical details, benchmarks, and what dedicated/private would look like.

[02:05] Samir: high level, are you prototyping, pilot, or full-prod? what's the timeline?
[02:12] Priya: we want pilot q1 27, production by q2. core requirement: sub-200ms 95th for ranker call, and embeddings refresh window shouldn't exceed 30s for hot items.
[02:28] Jenna: okay that's helpful — just to clarify, is that 200ms including vector DB lookup + rerank?
[02:33] Priya: yes — end-to-end. currently we do a fanout of 10 nearest neighbors per shard then rerank with a small LLM.

[05:10] Liam: short stack: we use milvus today for vector store, self-hosted k8s. considering pinecone as managed but concerned about cost. also thinking about switching to a hybrid approach where hot items are cached in memstore.
[05:25] Samir: got it — common pattern. our platform can run hosted (simple), dedicated pools (predictable throughput), or private in your VPC. for milvus we do standard connectors — Jenna can speak to latency and caching.

[07:00] Jenna: on caching: redwood supports automatic prefix / kv cache for autoregressive flows and we have embedding-level cache for short-lived hot keys — it's configurable per-route. staleness is a policy thing: you can set TTLs or invalidate on write.
[07:16] Priya: when you say invalidate on write, is that immediate across replicas? we have a near-real-time pipeline so writes happen a lot.
[07:24] Jenna: yes, with dedicated/ private you can get faster invalidation guarantees because we control the routing; hosted has eventual invalidation based on your TTL but we can also push webhooks to invalidate on your write if you want near-immediate. there's a networking hop though.

[09:40] Marco: and what's the cost delta? if we keep a short TTL and hit the model more often that could blow up cost vs keeping a slightly stale cache.
[09:50] Samir: exactly the tradeoff — we typically model this as request rate x miss rate x model cost. we can simulate with your traffic to show sweet spot.

[12:12] Priya: on embeddings dims: current vectors are 1024d (float32) from our encoder. are you recommending quantization?
[12:20] Jenna: for throughput, quantizing to 8-bit or 4-bit ints for ANN is common — it drops RAM and improves fanout latency. tradeoff is small accuracy delta; we can run quantization-aware evals. also per-route you can use a smaller dim for fast retrieval then rerank with full model.
[14:00] Liam: i want to understand tail latency. our worst-case is spiky traffic when promotions roll out. do you auto-scale dedicated pools?
[14:09] Samir: yes — dedicated supports autoscaling plus burst capacity; private can be autoscaled if you tie it to your infra, but the difference is control vs cost predictability. hosted scales but there can be multi-tenant variability at 99.99th.

[16:30] Priya: what about vector DB integration specifics — connectors to milvus? will we need adapters?
[16:38] Jenna: we have native connectors for some stores, milvus among them, but often customers use a lightweight adapter that handles sharding/fanout logic. if you want to keep existing milvus we can do an adapter and implement fallback to a cached index in the redwood runtime for hot keys.

[19:05] Marco: curious about consistency: if we write a new vector and immediately score it, what's realistic for a hosted deployment?
[19:12] Jenna: hosted: typical eventual visibility 1–3s for objects that pipeline pushes, depending on your ingestion path; with webhooks we can invalidate caches quicker. dedicated/private where you control network/storage can reach sub-second consistent visibility. but if you're writing 10s per second you'll need to benchmark.

[21:40] Liam: okay so for pilot, we need a benchmark that covers: base retrieval latencies, miss rate under TTLs, rerank model cost, and end-to-end 95/99 percentiles.
[21:51] Jenna: yes — propose a matrix: vary TTLs (5s, 30s, 60s), vary fanout (5,10,20), and measure cost & tail latency. we'll also test quantized vs full dims.

[24:10] Priya: can redwood run the ANN locally for the test, or do we need to mirror our milvus?
[24:17] Jenna: we can run a test harness against both — you can point to your milvus snapshot and we'll also run an in-memory cache path on redwood to mimic warm keys. that gives direct apples-to-apples latency.

[27:00] Marco: security — we need SOC2 + SSO, and for private deployment KMS integration. also residency: EU data must stay in eu-west-1.
[27:12] Samir: we have SOC2 docs and HSM/KMS options for private. for hosted, we can restrict region and we support bring-your-own-key via our private offering. we'll send the compliance pack.

[29:30] Liam: what about observability? we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and a breakdown of model vs retrieval cost.
[29:38] Jenna: console exposes per-route token and latency breakdowns, traces, and we can stream logs to your datadog/splunk. for dedicated you get longer retention as part of the package.

[32:10] Priya: recommend a strategy: hot cache for top 1% of items with 5–30s TTL, cold store in milvus with longer TTL, rerank only when vector similarity passes a threshold. thoughts?
[32:23] Jenna: that's a good design pattern. suffix: use a small LRU in-memory cache in front of the retrieval to eliminate network hops, then fallback to vendor milvus. also add probabilistic warming for predicted hot items.

[35:05] Marco: any gotchas with quantized embeddings and rerank? we need to ensure rerank uses full precision otherwise quality drops.
[35:13] Jenna: yes, do retrieval on quantized for speed then warm rerank with full-precision embeddings fed into the reranker or run reranker model on full tokens. keep an eval set to detect regressions.

[38:50] Liam: cost ballparks: can you give a quick example of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private cost shape?
[38:58] Samir: crude example — hosted: pay-per-request variable, good for early stages; dedicated: monthly baseline + lower per-token; private: license + infra ops cost but best for data residency and audit needs. we'll send a detailed one-pager with numbers based on your traffic.

[42:00] Priya: one operational question — how do we handle write amplification when we push new embeddings at 10m granularity for hot items, do you throttle writes?
[42:10] Jenna: we support batching and coalescing writes inside our ingestion, plus you can set up a write buffer and apply dedupe by item id. for high-write workloads, dedicated/private reduces IO contention.

[45:30] Marco: ok, let's talk pilot success criteria: 95th latency <200ms, embedding freshness <30s for hot items, cost per 1M requests under $X (we'll share X). if you can hit that with a dedicated config, we consider private for prod.
[45:46] Samir: perfect — we'll use that as target. Jenna will produce benchmark plan and we'll map it to hosted/dedicated/private scenarios.

[48:00] Priya: quick note — our current embedding size is 1024 float32, we plan to try 512 and quantize — expect small quality delta.
[48:10] Jenna: we'll include quantization sweep in the plan.

[50:20] Liam: next steps recap?
[50:25] Samir: yep — i'll send hosting one-pager and pricing. jenna drafts benchmark. priya shares traffic and refresh cadence. we'll send security docs. plan to regroup after you review by early jan.
[50:40] Marco: sounds good. thanks all.
[50:42] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and action items. bye.

End of transcript.
